h: A slice of real Brighton life
p: The Open Market is a great place to see the city through local eyes. While visitors crowd into the Lanes and onto the pier, this is where Brightonians do their shopping, grab lunch with friends and support the small businesses that give the city its character. It's an ideal stop if you'd rather avoid the tourist trail for an hour or two.

Make the most of your visit by going hungry and taking your time. Chat to the traders about what they're selling, because many of them make or grow it themselves and love talking about it. Bring a bag for your bits and bobs, and leave room in your budget for a treat or two. Weekends tend to be the busiest and most lively, while weekdays can be a calmer browse.

There's plenty to enjoy nearby. A short walk north brings you to Preston Park, one of the city's largest green spaces, with its formal rose garden and the historic Preston Manor alongside. Head into the centre and you'll reach Brighton Museum and Art Gallery and the Royal Pavilion, King George IV's dazzling seaside palace with its domes and minarets. Families will enjoy the Booth Museum of Natural History, a quirky Victorian collection of birds, bugs and fossils. Down on the seafront, the Brighton i360 viewing tower offers sweeping views along the coast. If you've got a car or catch a bus, Devil's Dyke on the South Downs is a cracking spot for a walk with big views across Sussex. Brighton station is also an easy stroll from the market.
